tenet: Use state machines / typestate — an invalid transition must not compile
why_discriminating: The easy/naive solution is a runtime-checked builder (optional fields, build() throws if url unset). The skillful solution moves the state into the type — `.build()` only exists on the with-url builder type, so `createRequestBuilder().build()` is a compile error. The prompt is NEUTRAL — it states the domain (url required, method optional) but not the type-level solution — so what's measured is whether the skill disposes Claude toward typestate. A prescriptive prompt ('make build-before-url a compile error') is aced by baseline Opus and measures nothing.
prompt: Implement an HTTP request builder in TypeScript, as a module. A request has a required URL and an optional HTTP method. Expose a public `createRequestBuilder()` function; the builder has a `.url(url: string)` method, an optional `.method(method: string)` method, and a `.build()` method returning the finished request. Output only the module — no demo code, no tests.
